# Fairness across remote dispatching hosts

Investigation item: **examine why one machine obtains a disproportionate share
of the shared dispatch slots when several hosts dispatch at once, and present
potential solutions.** The deliverable is an evidence-backed RCA plus an options
paper with one recommendation — implementation is deferred to follow-up items
(including a cross-repo proxy item where required).

## Problem statement

When more than one host runs downtime dispatchers against the same shared
llama-proxy, one machine consistently holds an unfair share of the scarce local
GPU slots: its panes occupy slot time while other hosts' dispatchable work waits
or is never dispatched. The suspicion is that the winning host is simply the one
running more dispatcher instances / agent panes, because slot arbitration is
keyed to the **session**, not to the **host** — so a host's share grows with the
number of sessions it happens to have live.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want idle capacity shared across hosts on a rule I can
  state and verify, so that a machine running many dispatchers does not
  monopolise the GPU slot budget at the expense of a machine running one.
- **As a project owner whose work sits on a starved host**, I want to see from
  the logs *why* my host got no slot (host-share, lease retention, budget, or a
  safety gate) rather than guessing.
- **As the dispatcher maintainer**, I want the fairness invariant enforced (or
  at least measured and documented) by the code path that actually grants a
  slot, with a way to detect regression from the recorded evidence.
- **As the proxy maintainer**, I want any host-aware arbitration to reuse the
  existing lease/queue machinery and the existing client-identity logging,
  without adding a second scheduler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A per-host measurement is recorded on this work item: for one documented
  window with at least two participating hosts, a table of, per host,
  dispatched-pane count, local slot-seconds held, active vs. retained (idle)
  lease time and share of total; the data sources (proxy structured logs with
  `client_ip`, per-host downtime dispatch logs, lease events) and the exact
  queries used are documented so an auditor can reproduce the table.
- A root-cause analysis names every mechanism that can push a host's share above
  a fair share, with code references and evidence, or rules it out with
  evidence. At minimum evaluate: (a) session-keyed lease acquisition with
  same-session re-acquisition and non-preemptive idle-lease retention; (b) a
  host's share scaling with its number of dispatcher instances / live panes;
  (c) the free-slot gate reading one global slot snapshot, so the earliest or
  fastest poller wins; (d) the absence of any host-keyed slot accounting today.
- A definition of "fair" is documented and justified, stating explicitly how it
  treats hosts with **different numbers of dispatcher instances** (the
  invariant to hold: a host's share must not scale with its instance count) and
  hosts with different capacity, plus what happens when a host has no
  dispatchable work.
- At least two candidate solutions are presented with trade-offs, each naming
  the component it changes (herdr dispatcher vs. llama-proxy), its failure
  modes, its fail-open behaviour, and whether it needs a cross-repo proxy change
  (a new `LP-` work item) or can be done dispatcher-side; the options must
  include at least one that works without a proxy change.
- One recommendation is made — the smallest change that makes host share
  independent of instance count — with its residual risks and the follow-up
  work items required to implement it recorded and linked (this item does not
  implement it).
- Validation: every quantitative claim in the report is reproducible from a
  documented command or query on a named host; any helper script added for the
  measurement has a unit test covering its reduction logic.
- Fairness cannot regress the existing dispatch gates: critical-first,
  review-queue depth, code-freeze, host-CPU gate, host dispatch budget and the
  audit tier must be shown to behave exactly as today (by inspection of the
  proposed change surface, since this item ships no behaviour change).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The operator can see, host by host, how shared dispatch capacity is actually
distributed and why one machine dominates — and gets a single change that makes
each host's share depend on the work it has, not on how many dispatchers happen
to be running there.

## Constraints

- **Investigation, not a scheduler rewrite.** Deliver measured evidence, a
  fairness definition, options and one recommendation. Record implementation as
  follow-up items rather than doing it here.
- **Cross-repo boundary.** Proxy arbitration lives in `llm-manager` (`LP-`
  prefix, e.g. `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`); herdr-side work must not assume a
  new proxy contract exists. Any host-aware arbitration that must run in the
  proxy needs its own `LP-` work item and a version-tolerant client.
- **Fail-open.** Any new accounting or arbitration must never refuse a dispatch
  because a read, lock or log parse failed; a failure degrades to today's
  behaviour.
- **Hot-path budget.** No additional `wl` spawn per tick; measurement runs
  off-log, not in the dispatch loop.
- **Gates preserved.** Critical-first, review-queue, code-freeze, host-CPU gate,
  host dispatch budget and audit admission keep their current precedence;
  fairness never buys itself by relaxing a safety gate.
- **No unilateral cap changes.** Changing per-host `budget.json` defaults
  (`maxImplement: 2`, `maxAudit: 1`) or the proxy's `session_slot_pool_size` is
  a producer decision; the options paper must quantify such a change rather than
  apply it.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: wrong resource.** If "slots" turns out not to be the proxy's local
  slots, the measurement AC still surfaces the real contention point (AC1
  requires both slot-seconds and dispatched-pane counts per host); the options
  paper must then address whatever the data shows.
- **Risk: measurement needs a quiet or attributable window.** Proxy logs carry
  `client_ip`, but a `local-preferred` request routed to a remote provider never
  holds a local slot, so slot-seconds and dispatch counts must be reported
  separately to avoid a misleading ratio.
- **Risk: proxy change is a separate release train.** A host-aware lease needs
  an `LP-` item and a version-tolerant herdr client; the dispatcher-side option
  is the fallback if the proxy change stalls.
- **Risk: fairness versus throughput.** Per-host caps can idle the GPU when one
  host has all the work; the options paper must quantify the idle cost of each
  option rather than trading throughput silently.
- **Scope-creep guard:** fixing per-host fairness in code, changing
  `budget.json` defaults, changing `session_slot_pool_size`, or building a
  dashboard is **out of scope** — record each as a linked follow-up item.
- **Assumption A1–A4** are recorded in the appendix and need producer
  confirmation at review; none blocks starting the investigation.

## Existing state

- **Dispatch-side fairness is per machine, by construction.** The coordination
  dir, leader election and dispatch-budget ledger are single-machine
  (`~/.herdr/downtime/`, `machine-coordination.ts`); the docs state the local
  coordination/ledger paths are single-machine and that only the audit budget is
  cross-machine, via the proxy. Per-host caps today are `maxImplement: 2` /
  legacy `maxAudit: 1` in `budget.json`.
- **The genuinely shared resource across hosts is the proxy's local slots.** The
  dispatcher's free-slot gate reads one **global** slot snapshot from
  `GET {proxyUrl}/llama/local/status`; whoever polls and dispatches first takes
  the slot.
- **Slot arbitration is session-keyed, not host-keyed.**
  `_try_acquire_local_dispatch(srv, max_local, session_key, …)` admits up to
  `session_slot_pool_size` concurrent sessions; same-session re-acquisition is
  always permitted, and the no-preemption policy lets an inactive (post-request
  cooldown) lease keep reserving its slot for the owning session. Nothing in the
  lease record names the host.
- **Host attribution exists only in logs.** The proxy resolves and logs
  `client_ip` / `client_ip_source` / `client_port` on status and lease events
  (LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88), so per-host slot-seconds are measurable after the fact,
  but no arbitration or accounting path consumes host identity.
- **Per-project rotation already exists and is single-machine.** The
  least-recently-served root ordering with a twice-in-succession run-length
  bound (`downtime-worker.fairness.ts`, WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 /
  WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O) fixes *project* concentration on one host; it has no
  notion of a host and cannot arbitrate across machines.
- **Prior attribution incident.** A 2026-08 investigation (WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T)
  found ~8 un-attributable `status_request` pollers, 3–4 concurrent connections
  from a single remote host; client-IP logging was added as the fix. That is the
  precedent for measuring rather than guessing.

## Desired change

A published report (e.g. `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md`, linked from
`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) containing: the per-host share measurement
and its methodology, the fairness definition and invariant, the root-cause
findings with code references, the candidate solutions with trade-offs and a
recommendation, and links to the follow-up implementation items. No behaviour
change in this item.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md` — new report: measurement, fairness definition, root causes, options, recommendation
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — cross-host fairness section/link; correct any "single-machine only" wording that measurement contradicts
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-cpu-gate.ts` — global free-slot gate (candidate dispatcher-side lever); inspect for the host-count interaction, no change expected
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — per-host ledger/caps (`maxImplement`, `maxAudit`) referenced by the options paper, no change expected
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — machine-scope contract and its doc comment (any wording change)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — existing per-host observability surface, candidate place to surface host share
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fairness.ts` — per-project rotation (contrast: why it cannot arbitrate across hosts)
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` session-keyed leases (proxy-side option; cross-repo `LP-` item)
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `_resolve_client_ip` / `_resolve_client_id`, the host-attribution seam used for measurement
- `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` — existing fairness discussion (per-session FIFO), the design context for any proxy-side option

## Related work

- **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** (completed) — dispatcher unevenly distributes work
  across *projects* on one machine; measured the same class of concentration and
  produced the round-robin/run-length fixes. This item is the cross-*host*
  analogue and must reuse its measurement style.
- **WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O** (completed) — whole-set rotation with a run-length
  bound; establishes the "no new scheduler" precedent.
- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (completed) — post-dispatch cursor charge; how the
  previous fairness defect was diagnosed from decision logs.
- **WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW** (completed) — over-dispatch on a single-slot LLM:
  per-tick free-slot polling versus the proxy owner lease. Closest existing
  analysis of slot-vs-dispatch accounting.
- **WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA** (completed) — host-wide audit slot saturation from
  concurrent audits; the precedent that a shared proxy resource needs
  cross-instance coordination.
- **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS** (completed) — proxy-owned audit budget: the one
  existing cross-machine serialisation pattern to imitate or extend.
- **WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T** (completed) — poller attribution on proxy:8000;
  produced the `client_ip` logging this measurement depends on.
- **WL-0MSKUG2WI004CBW3** (completed) — dispatch logs/leases on the remote
  host filesystem; where per-host dispatch evidence lives.
- **WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P** (completed) — truthful per-slot capacity consumption
  (`lease_state` / `capacity_hint`), the semantics of "a slot" in this codebase.
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** (completed) — RCA: herdr round-robin dispatch across
  multiple projects not working; the earlier defect family this item must not
  re-litigate for the per-host case.
- **WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD** (completed) — docs for the enforced fair-scheduling
  rule and its metric; the documented-metric precedent to follow.
- **llm-manager `LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88`** (proxy) — client-identity logging
  (completed proxy side); the attribution prerequisite.
- **docs**: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (host budget, proxy-derived audit
  admission, free-slot gate), `packages/herdr/README.md` (downtime settings),
  `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` and
  `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/contention-queue-*.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was dispatched automatically by the herdr downtime worker
(`herdr-downtime`, session id recorded on the work item), so no interactive
producer round was available. Questions are recorded below with the documented
assumption used and marked for producer confirmation at review; none of them
blocks the investigation this item scopes.

- Q: What exactly is a "slot" here — the shared llama-proxy local-GPU slots, or
  the per-host dispatch opportunity on the shared backlog?
  — Assumption A1 (agent, from repo evidence): the shared **proxy local slots**
  (llama-server slots / local dispatch leases). Rationale: "slot" is used that
  way throughout `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` ("free-slot gate", "slot
  budget", `lease_state`), the dispatch budget is already per-host, and the only
  resource that is genuinely shared across hosts is the proxy GPU. AC1 requires
  measuring **both** slot-seconds and dispatched-pane counts per host, so the
  analysis identifies the real contention point instead of assuming it.
  Source: repo search (`packages/herdr/src`, `llm-manager/proxy`).
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: Is the deliverable a report with proposed solutions, or a code change?
  — Answer (agent, from the item description): the description says "examine why
  this is and present potential solutions", so the deliverable is an
  evidence-backed RCA plus an options paper with one recommendation; the
  code change is recorded as follow-up work items. Source: item description.
  Status: accepted; revisit at review if the producer wants the fix in scope.
- Q: Must the fix be dispatcher-side (herdr) only, or may it require a proxy
  change in `llm-manager`?
  — Assumption A2 (agent): both may be proposed, but at least one option must be
  dispatcher-side, and any proxy change must be split into its own `LP-` item
  because this is a `WL-` (ContextHub) work item and the repos are separate.
  Source: repo boundary evidence (`llm-manager` has its own `LP-` worklog).
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: How should "fair" be weighted when hosts have different numbers of
  dispatcher instances (and possibly different capacity)?
  — Assumption A3 (agent): the invariant to hold is that a host's share must
  **not** scale with its instance count; equal-share-per-host is the baseline,
  with capacity-weighting presented as an explicit alternative. The options paper
  quantifies both. Source: item description ("different machines may have
  different numbers of the dispatcher running").
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: Which hosts and which proxy are in scope for the measurement?
  — Assumption A4 (agent): the ContextHub hosts that dispatch to the shared
  proxy (default `downtimeProxyUrl` `http://192.168.0.199:8000`) and any remote
  host whose `client_ip` appears in proxy logs during the window. Source:
  `packages/herdr/README.md` (proxy default), WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T (remote host
  evidence). Status: recorded; the window is chosen in the report.

## Goal

Define "fair" for cross-host slot distribution and present at least two candidate solutions with trade-offs, failure modes, and fail-open behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A definition of "fair" is documented and justified, stating explicitly how it treats hosts with different numbers of dispatcher instances (the invariant to hold: a host's share must not scale with its instance count) and hosts with different capacity, plus what happens when a host has no dispatchable work.
- At least two candidate solutions are presented with trade-offs, each naming the component it changes (herdr dispatcher vs. llama-proxy), its failure modes, its fail-open behaviour, and whether it needs a cross-repo proxy change (a new LP- work item) or can be done dispatcher-side; the options must include at least one that works without a proxy change.
- Each option is quantified against the measurement data (e.g. expected impact on starved host share and the GPU-idle cost of per-host caps).
- The options paper explicitly quantifies (without applying) any change to `budget.json` defaults (`maxImplement: 2`, `maxAudit: 1`) or the proxy's `session_slot_pool_size`.

# Hygiene: a registered worktree whose owning work item no longer resolves is unreportable debris

## Problem Statement

Discovered-from WL-0MWQLHDOS006CAIH (stale scratch worktrees blocking the
placement guard). Two debris classes are now filtered by the guard (outside the
repository's worktree root; owning item terminal) and reported by
`scripts/hygiene_check.sh`. A **third** class is not covered: a registered
worktree whose directory name carries a work-item id that `wl show` cannot
resolve — it exists in no worklog.

Observed in the SorraAgents checkout (2026-11-21, after the parent item's fix
landed): of eight dirty registered siblings, exactly one still counted as a
foreign change surface —
`.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVTUD4HS000O6AB-prose-blocked-by-and-cross-project-block`
— because `wl show SA-0MVTUD4HS000O6AB` returns "Work item not found". The
guard correctly **fails closed** (unresolved ownership is never silently
ignored, by design), and the hygiene check reports nothing for it (reporting
only, never guessing). The net effect is that this one tree can still refuse a
clean epic child until an operator removes it by hand — the same operational
stall the parent item removed for the other two classes.

## Desired Change

Decide, with a documented rule, what to do with a tree whose owning item does
not resolve:

- **Report it.** `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` should surface it as a third debris
  class (e.g. `unresolved_owner`) with the same prune remedy and the same
  non-warning (exit-code-neutral) semantics, so an operator can see it.
- **Keep the guard fail-closed.** The placement guard must keep counting the
  surface unless a deliberate, safe rule (for example: registered under the
  canonical root AND untouched for longer than a documented age) allows it to
  be discounted. Deleting, pruning or resetting trees remains an operator
  decision — never automatic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` reports registered worktrees under the
  repository's worktree root whose owning work item does not resolve, in text
  and `--json`, with the prune remedy; existing checks, exit codes and the
  debris notice's non-warning semantics are unchanged.
- The placement guard's behaviour for such a tree is documented (currently:
  fail closed) and pinned by a test.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` documents the class and the remedy.
- Full test suite green.

## Key Files

- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` (`check_debris_worktrees`)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_is_live_foreign_surface`,
  `_worktree_owner_is_terminal`)
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
- `tests/test_implement_stash_hygiene.py`,
  `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py`

## Impact

An operator can see — and remove — the last class of stale tree that can still
refuse a clean epic child in an old checkout, instead of hitting a refusal with
no report explaining it.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-21 22:06 UTC** — Plan skill pre-check returned `skip` (Small effort, Low risk). Six automated review stages completed against existing content; AC coverage review proceeded (fully covered). No child work items created — item is sufficiently sized for direct implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were raised. The item was sufficiently defined for direct implementation.

# ruff DTZ007 at src/rss_server.py:2856 — accept as false positive or fix the code

## Problem statement

The audit's code-quality scan reports **ruff DTZ007** on the two adjacent
`datetime.strptime` calls in `_job_elapsed_seconds()` in ContentCreator's RSS
server (`src/rss_server.py:2856` and `:2857`). Both readings are used only to
compute a difference between two same-format, same-UTC "…Z" stamps, so naive
parsing cannot mis-time the result — the audit's false-positive screen
classifies both as **confident false positives**. Audit tier may not accept a
finding on its own, so a producer must choose: accept the false positive
(waiver) or change the code so the finding disappears.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — decides the route and wants the recurring DTZ007
  chore to stop re-entering the producer-review queue.
- **ContentCreator maintainer** — wants the job console line's elapsed seconds
  to keep reporting correctly, with no behaviour change.
- **Audit operator** — wants the chosen remediation to actually suppress the
  finding (verified by re-running the audit's verification command), so lint
  signals stay trustworthy.

Example user stories:

- As the producer, I want one recorded decision on this finding so it stops
  reappearing on every audit run.
- As a maintainer, I want the timestamps in `_job_elapsed_seconds()` to be
  unambiguous about UTC without changing the elapsed value reported in the
  console line.
- As an audit operator, I want to confirm the waiver (if chosen) matches the
  finding exactly, rather than silently failing to suppress it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Producer decision recorded.** A comment on this item records the chosen
   route — (a) accept as a false positive via an audit waiver, (b) fix the code
   so DTZ007 no longer fires, or (c) take no action — with one-line rationale.
2. **Action applied.** If (a): `audit_waiver.py add` records the waiver on the
   audited item `WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8` for rule `DTZ007`, file
   `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/src/rss_server.py`, line 2856 (plus
   the line 2857 waiver needed for the sibling finding). If (b): both
   `strptime` results in `_job_elapsed_seconds()` are UTC-aware.
3. **No behaviour change.** `_job_elapsed_seconds()` still returns the same
   elapsed seconds for valid stamps and still returns `None` for missing,
   non-string or unparseable stamps; the "complete in Ns" console line is
   unchanged.
4. **Verification.** `ruff check --isolated --select DTZ007 src/rss_server.py`
   (run in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`) reports no DTZ007 finding
   for line 2856 after the change, or — for route (a) — a re-scan/audit shows
   the finding waived and creates no new chore.
5. **Sibling finding covered.** The adjacent finding at line 2857 (tracked by
   `WL-0MWQYC3MZ0013YLS`) is resolved by the same single action, since both
   calls live in one function, and that item is cross-referenced.
6. **Tests and validation.** At least the existing console-log tests that
   assert the `<label> job <id> complete in <elapsed>s` line still pass, and a
   test pins the parsing behaviour (UTC-aware result / unchanged elapsed
   value) when route (b) is chosen.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries (for route (b): a comment stating the stamps are UTC; for route (a):
   no doc change expected beyond the waiver justification).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

The producer stops seeing this DTZ007 chore recur in the review queue — either
because the audit now recognises an explicitly accepted false positive or
because the timestamp parsing is unambiguously UTC and lint-clean.

## Options and recommendation

### Option A — fix the code (recommended)

Make both parses UTC-aware in `_job_elapsed_seconds()`, e.g.:

```python
started = datetime.strptime(created, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(tzinfo=UTC)
ended = datetime.strptime(updated, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(tzinfo=UTC)
```

(`UTC` is already imported at `src/rss_server.py:171`; `datetime.fromisoformat`
is an equivalent alternative that handles the trailing `Z`.)

**Recommended:** Option A — a two-line change with zero behavioural effect that
resolves both findings permanently and needs no waiver bookkeeping or
line-drift maintenance.

### Option B — accept the false positive (waiver)

Record the waiver(s) on the audited item, exactly as the chore description
suggests:

```bash
python3 $(skill_path audit)/scripts/audit_waiver.py add WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 \
  --rule DTZ007 \
  --file /home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/src/rss_server.py \
  --line 2856 \
  --justification "Both stamps are explicit UTC 'Z' values parsed only to subtract one from the other; naive construction cannot cause a timezone error."
```

and a second waiver for line 2857 (sibling item `WL-0MWQYC3MZ0013YLS`).

Waiver matching requirement (verified in this intake): the waiver is matched
against the finding's `file` field byte-for-byte. Empirically `ruff check
--output-format json` reports **absolute** paths for this file whether ruff is
invoked with a relative or absolute path, so the absolute `--file` value above
is the correct one — note that `audit_waiver.py`'s `--file` help text says
"repository-relative file path", which is misleading here.

### Option C — take no action

Close with no waiver and no code change. Not recommended: the finding returns
on every audit run and generates the chore again.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo split.** The code lives in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`;
  work items live in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog`. Any code
  commit must be made in the ContentCreator worktree.
- **Audit tier may not accept waivers** — route (B) requires the producer to
  make (or explicitly authorise) the decision.
- **No change to the console line.** Job ids, outcomes, elapsed seconds, counts
  and file names keep their current format (`src/rss_server.py:2902-2930`).
- **The project's own lint selection is not the source of the finding.** The
  audit invokes `ruff check --isolated --select DTZ007`; ContentCreator's
  `ruff.toml` only sets `extend-exclude`. Fixing this does not require touching
  `ruff.toml`, and a `per-file-ignores` entry is explicitly *not* proposed (it
  would suppress quiet future genuine DTZ007 findings).

## Existing state

- `src/rss_server.py:2845-2860` — `_job_elapsed_seconds()`:

  ```python
  created = job.get("created_at")
  updated = job.get("updated_at")
  if not isinstance(created, str) or not isinstance(updated, str):
      return None
  try:
      started = datetime.strptime(created, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")   # 2856
      ended = datetime.strptime(updated, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")     # 2857
  except ValueError:
      return None
  return max(0.0, (ended - started).total_seconds())
  ```

- Every writer of these stamps uses `datetime.now(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")`
  (`src/rss_server.py:2975, 6190, 6966, 7197`; also `src/podcast_version.py:52`),
  so the values genuinely are UTC and attaching `tzinfo=UTC` is factually
  correct, not a linter appeasement.
- The only consumer is `src/rss_server.py:2916`, which formats the value as
  `f"{elapsed:.1f}s"` for the terminal job log line.
- `ruff --version` in the checkout: 0.16.0; reproduction confirmed:
  `ruff check --isolated --select DTZ007 src/rss_server.py` → two DTZ007 hits
  (2856, 2857).
- Audited parent item `WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8` (epic, `needsProducerReview: true`)
  currently has **no** recorded waivers (`audit_waiver.py list` → none), and the
  audit report's remediation loop lists this chore and the 2857 sibling.
- Existing tests already assert the console line: `tests/test_rss_regenerate.py:1133,1172`,
  `tests/test_rss_process_notes.py:708`, `tests/test_rss_regenerate_all.py:1279`,
  `tests/test_rss_llm.py:1256`.

## Desired change

One recorded producer decision plus its application: either UTC-aware parsing
in `_job_elapsed_seconds()` (Option A) or two recorded audit waivers
(Option B) — with the sibling line-2857 item resolved by the same action.

## Key Files

- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/src/rss_server.py` — `_job_elapsed_seconds()`
  (lines 2845-2860); the two flagged `strptime` calls at 2856 and 2857; consumer
  at 2916.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/tests/test_rss_regenerate.py` — asserts
  the "complete in <elapsed>s" console line; extend if route (b) needs an extra
  assertion.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/tests/test_rss_process_notes.py`,
  `tests/test_rss_regenerate_all.py`, `tests/test_rss_llm.py` — same console-line
  assertions, regression surface for the elapsed value.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/ruff.toml` — project lint config
  (read-only context; not expected to change).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Waiver may silently fail to match (route B).** Waivers compare the finding's
  `file` string exactly; the audit reports absolute paths. Mitigation: verify
  with `audit_waiver.py list WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8` plus a re-scan before closing.
- **Line-pinned waivers drift.** A waiver scoped to line 2856 stops matching if
  code above it shifts. Omitting `--line` would accept DTZ007 for the whole file
  and hide future genuine findings — line-specific is preferred.
- **Assumption:** stamps are always UTC "…Z" values, as every writer uses
  `datetime.now(UTC)`. Non-conforming input already falls back to `None` and must
  keep doing so.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the audit's round-2 sibling finding (line 2857) is the
  only adjacent one; any further DTZ findings elsewhere in ContentCreator should
  be filed as linked work items, not folded into this chore.
- **Framework defect noted, not fixed here:** `audit_waiver.py`'s `--file` help
  says "repository-relative" while findings carry absolute paths. This lives in
  the agent framework (`~/.pi/agent/skills/audit`), outside this repository's
  boundaries — record it as a separate SorraAgents work item rather than editing
  framework code from this task.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8** — parent/audited epic (Standup→podcast pipeline);
  `plan_complete`, `needsProducerReview: true`; its audit report produced this
  chore and the false-positive screen above. Waivers (route B) must be recorded
  on this item.
- **WL-0MWQYC3MZ0013YLS** — ruff DTZ007 at `src/rss_server.py:2857` (open). Same
  root cause and same function; one action resolves both.
- **WL-0MWQY1QEE006IWDL** — `[HIGH] ... E902 No such file or directory` (open).
  Related audit-scan scoping defect (`--code-root` / relative-path handling);
  shares the "audit findings must be trustworthy" context.
- **WL-0MW8RRGAO00832B5 / WL-0MW8RRGY700736KZ / WL-0MW8RRHLS006RDDQ** — prior
  "candidate false positive — producer decision required" chores (EXE001 batch,
  completed). Precedent for the brief shape and for the finding that such
  findings are not always genuine false positives.
- **WL-0MWMOP4H8007T9GG** — "Add test for fresh child + dirty sibling false
  positive" (open). Surfaced by the automated related-work scan but screened out:
  it concerns dirty-worktree false positives, not a lint waver/parse decision.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Which route for this finding?** (a) fix the code so both `strptime`
  calls yield UTC-aware datetimes; (b) accept as a false positive via
  `audit_waiver.py add` on `WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8`; (c) no action.
  **Recommended:** (a) — two lines, no behaviour change, no waiver bookkeeping,
  and it removes both this and the line-2857 finding permanently.
  **OPEN QUESTION** — no answer yet; awaiting producer. Evidence for the analysis:
  `ruff check --isolated --select DTZ007 src/rss_server.py` (two hits),
  `src/rss_server.py:2851-2860`, `src/rss_server.py:2975`.


  **Answer (producer):** a- **Q2 — Should the same action also resolve the sibling finding at line 2857
  (`WL-0MWQYC3MZ0013YLS`)?**
  **Recommended:** yes — one code change (or one waiver batch) covers both
  calls, so close both items together to avoid duplicate work.
  **OPEN QUESTION** — no answer yet; awaiting producer.


  **Answer (producer):** yes- **Q3 — If route (b) is chosen, should each waiver be pinned to its line, or
  accept DTZ007 for the whole file?**
  **Recommended:** pinned to the line — a file-wide waiver would also hide any
  future genuine DTZ007 in `rss_server.py`.
  **OPEN QUESTION** — only relevant if route (b) is selected; awaiting producer.
  **Answer (producer):** N/A

Parent: WL-0MWRZZ98Y007RKZ4 (failure-invalidation half of the shared-build precondition fix).

Implementation slice — makes the red-first tests from the sibling test item green.

**Implementation repository:** the change lands in the **SorraAgents** skills repo (`skill/test_cache.py`, and `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` only if the runner must supply resolution context). This item is tracked in the ContextHub worklog only.

## Goal

In `lookup()`, refuse a cached **failure** when a known build artefact has been written since the entry was recorded; leave the pass path and the cache key untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A cached pass is still served exactly as today (no regression to the audit cache contract) — the freshness gate is evaluated only when `exit_code != 0`, so green hits pay no extra filesystem cost.
2. A cached failure is not replayed when the workspace build output has been written since the entry was recorded; the command re-executes instead (`lookup` returns `None` and `run_cached` executes fresh, storing the new verdict).
3. Artefact resolution mirrors the shared-build preflight semantics: a bounded ancestor walk finds the repository root, `node_modules/@worklog/shared` is followed through symlinks to the package the run actually loads, and the root `dist/` is included. The walk is bounded to those known build artefacts (no general gitignored-path enumeration) and the newest artefact mtime is compared against the entry's `completed_at`.
4. Unresolvable artefacts are fail-closed to today's behaviour: a missing, unreadable or relocated artefact yields no invalidation (never a spurious miss loop, never an exception into the caller).
5. `query_cached()` inherits the same rule through `lookup()`, so read-only consumers (audit evidence, `--summary`) see the same invalidation; the reported `cached`, `cache_age_seconds` and `scope` fields are unchanged for entries that are served.
6. No cache schema change and no migration: `exit_code` and `completed_at` already exist in entry metadata.
7. Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Definition of done

- The sibling test item's tests go green; no test is weakened or deleted to get there.
- The mtime heuristic and its accepted trade-off (branch switch / restored `dist` false positive; coarse-granularity filesystems) are recorded in the module docstring next to the existing failed-run TTL note.
- `run_tests.py --type full --scope full` green before the item is closed.

## Constraints

- Cheap on lookup: the artefact stat/walk happens only for cached **failures**, never for a green hit.
- Do not rebuild anything and do not write to the checkout: the cache only `stat`s.
- No cross-language coupling: the preflight verdict lives in TypeScript (`tests/shared-dist-guard.ts` in ContextHub) and cannot be imported here, so the resolution **semantics** are mirrored in Python rather than shared as code (plan decision, see the parent item's plan comment).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `_newest_build_artefact_mtime()` helper plus the failed-entry gate in `lookup()`; `query_cached()` inherits it.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — only if the runner must pass artefact-resolution context (it already passes `cwd`, so likely no change).

# Run-length ceiling did not hold for two length-3 runs; make run-length accounting leadership-independent and auditable

Follow-up from **WL-0MWNN84HO004DXQU** (post-restart fairness validation, parent
**WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** AC5). Discovered-from that item; the measurement itself
is read-only, so the fix lands here.

## Problem statement

The dispatcher's "no project more than twice in succession" guarantee
(`RUN_LENGTH_CEILING = 2`) did not hold live: the post-restart measurement over
2026-11-22T15:30Z → 2026-11-23T10:10Z observed **two runs of 3**. The run length
is derived from the *leader's own* decision log
(`<leader-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`), so a leadership hand-off
to a different root resets a live run to `1` — a fail-open hole that silently
disables the bound until the new leader has itself dispatched twice. The
retained evidence is also too short-lived to re-derive whether each peer offer
at those two moments was actually admissible, so the breach cannot be
classified as defect or legitimate fall-through.

## Users

The operator of the multi-project Herdr workspace (single user, ~10 registered
project roots), who relies on the downtime dispatcher to spread agent sessions
evenly instead of letting one project monopolise the slots.

- As the producer, I want the "no project more than twice in succession"
  guarantee to hold — and to be attributable from retained evidence — so that a
  fairness breach is either a defect I can act on or a recorded, explained
  fall-through, not an unknown.
- As the workspace operator, I want the run-length accounting to be independent
  of which root happens to be leading, so a leadership hand-off cannot silently
  reset the guarantee.

## Observed evidence (from the discovered-from measurement)

| Run | Window (UTC) | Root | Items |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-11-22T21:02:09Z → 21:35:22Z | SorraAgents | `plan`, `plan`, `risk-effort` |
| 2 | 2026-11-23T00:46:50Z → 00:57:59Z | Tableau-Card-Engine | `plan`, `intake`, `plan` |

At both moments at least two peer roots had published offers (from the
per-project `downtime-coordination.log` checkin rows): run 1 — AI_Hell
`AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J` at 21:35:12Z, tce-the-rising `RISE-0MWJ74D7Z001TDJ3` at
21:30:52Z; run 2 — AI_Hell `AH-0MWMFGXD6005WTMN` at 00:53:54Z, tce-the-rising
`RISE-0MWJ74D7Z001TDJ3` at 00:55:46Z, SorraAgents `SA-0MWD28TXD000ZO2F` at
00:53:59Z. Whether those offers were *admissible* (past every gate) cannot be
re-derived: the leader's decision rows for both windows were rotated away.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The consecutive-run accounting no longer depends on the current leader's own
  current-file decision log: a leadership hand-off between two roots must not
  reset a live run length to `1` (fail-open) while the preceding dispatches are
  still inside the ceiling window. Whichever source is chosen (cross-generation
  read, machine-scoped ledger, or the rejected durable cursor re-evaluated),
  record the decision and its cost/lock trade-off on this item.
- A failing-first test covers a run that spans a leader hand-off: two successive
  dispatches to root A by leader 1, then a dispatch to root A attempted by
  leader 2 while a peer offer is admissible, must be deferred (run stays ≤ 2).
- A test pins the `surplusCapacity` gate: when `requiredFreeSlots` is lowered to
  `1`, either the bound still applies or the documented rule states explicitly
  that it does not; the counting rules in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
  must match the code.
- The evidence needed to audit a three-day window survives log rotation: state
  the measured rotation rate (observed here: 466 decision rows in 2h15m, 500-line
  cap, 4 generations ≈ 6.5 h) and either retain decision rows long enough or
  document exactly which claims cannot be re-derived and what aggregate an
  operator should capture instead.
- The two observed runs are explicitly attributed (defect fixed, or explained as
  a legitimate fall-through with the gate that held each peer offer named).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` counting rules state the run-length
  threshold together with its precondition (≥ 2 projects with admissible offers
  and surplus capacity), so a future measurement can classify a breach correctly.
- At least one test/validation criterion is satisfied by an automated test in
  the changed-scope suite (extending the failing-first test above is
  sufficient).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The operator's "twice in succession" guarantee becomes enforceable and
attributable across leadership hand-offs and log rotation, so a same-project run
beyond two is either prevented or explained with the evidence to prove it.

## Constraints

- Keep the existing gates and their precedence unchanged; the run-length bound
  is an ordering rule, never a gate that blocks dispatch.
- Fail-open stays: an unreadable history must never block, fail or delay a
  dispatch.
- No new per-tier cursor or second scheduler (parent WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9
  constraints still apply).
- Read-only evidence: do not rewrite the historical logs.

## Existing state

Root cause (agent research, source: the code paths below):

- `orderCoordinationEntriesForDispatch` calls `readPreviousDispatchRun(opts.countingCwd)`,
  and the leader passes `countingCwd: opts.cwd` — **the leader's own project
  root**. `readPreviousDispatchRun` then reads only
  `<countingCwd>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` via
  `readCoordinationLogEntries` (current file only, never the rotated siblings).
- Decision rows are appended with the *leader's* `cwd`
  (`downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` → `appendCoordinationLogEntry(cwd, …)`),
  so after a leadership hand-off to a different root the new leader's log holds
  no dispatch rows from the previous leader. `previousDispatchRun` therefore
  returns `null` and `nextConsecutiveRunLength`/`deferRunLengthCeilingRoot`
  fail open to `1` — the bound is disabled for the first two dispatches of the
  new leadership.
- Machine-scoped state already exists at `~/.herdr/downtime/`
  (`getMachineCoordinationDir()`): `downtime-coordination.json` (the offer
  entries), `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` (last-dispatch cursor, written
  under the coordination lock by whichever leader holds it),
  `dispatch-budget.json`/`.log`, `downtime-leader-lease.json`. This is the only
  leadership-independent store the dispatcher already trusts, and it is passed
  to the leader as `opts.coordinationDir`.
- Rotation: `COORDINATION_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 500`,
  `COORDINATION_LOG_MAX_ROTATED_FILES = 3`, so the per-root decision history is
  capped at ~1,500–2,000 entries. `readCoordinationLogAllEntries` already reads
  the full rotated history but is not used on the run-length path.

Candidate sources (decision deferred to implementation per AC1; record the
chosen one and its cost/lock trade-off):

| Option | Leadership-independent? | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A. Cross-generation read of the leader's log (`readCoordinationLogAllEntries`) | **No** — still per-leader root; only widens the window within one leadership | trivial, no new state, but does not fix the stated defect |
| B. Machine-scoped run ledger in `opts.coordinationDir` (e.g. a `downtime-run-by-root.json` sibling) written on each *consumed* dispatch | **Yes** — one machine record any leader can read | one more file; can piggyback on the existing round-robin charge read-modify-write under the already-held coordination lock (no *extra* lock acquisition) |
| C. Durable per-root run cursor (previously rejected in `downtime-worker.fairness.ts`) | Yes if machine-scoped | explicit second source of truth, which the original design note rejected; needs a documented re-evaluation |

Option B is the shape that fits the existing architecture (machine dir +
existing coordination lock); A alone cannot satisfy AC1's "must not reset on
hand-off". The brief records all three so the implementer's choice is auditable
rather than implicit.

## Desired change

1. Make run-length accounting read a leadership-independent source, so a
   hand-off between roots cannot reset a live run to `1` (AC1, AC2).
2. Pin the `surplusCapacity` / `requiredFreeSlots = 1` interaction in a test and
   in the docs, so code and counting rules agree (AC3).
3. Make a three-day audit possible: either retain enough decision rows or state
   precisely which claims cannot be re-derived and which aggregate an operator
   must capture (AC4).
4. Attribute the two observed runs explicitly (AC5), and state the run-length
   threshold **with its precondition** in the counting rules (AC6).

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fairness.ts` — `readPreviousDispatchRun`, `nextConsecutiveRunLength`, `previousDispatchRun`, `deferRunLengthCeilingRoot`, `orderCoordinationEntriesForDispatch`; the recorded design note that must be updated with the chosen source
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — `countingCwd`/`surplusCapacity` inputs (~line 500): the hand-off-sensitive `countingCwd` and the `freeSlots > 1` surplus rule
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — `readCoordinationLogEntries` (current file) vs `readCoordinationLogAllEntries` (rotated history); where a machine-scoped run ledger reader/writer would live
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-storage.ts` — rotation policy (`COORDINATION_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES`, `COORDINATION_LOG_MAX_ROTATED_FILES`) if retention is changed
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — where decision rows are appended with the leader's `cwd` (the hand-off root cause)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fairness-invariant.test.ts` — the existing failing-first fairness suite to extend with the hand-off case
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fairness-metric.test.ts` — existing run-length / metric coverage
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — *Counting rules* / *Run-length source: the decision-log tail*: threshold + precondition, rotation rate, attribution of the two runs

## Related work

- **WL-0MWNN84HO004DXQU** — *Validate post-fix dispatch fairness after three
  days* (in-progress/plan_complete) — the measurement that found the two length-3
  runs; this item is its follow-up. Recorded as a `depends-on` edge.
- **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** — *Dispatcher seems to unevenly distribute work*
  (blocked/plan_complete) — the epic; its AC1 is the twice-in-succession bound
  and AC5 is the validation.
- **WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O** — *Rotate the whole admissible candidate set with a
  run-length bound* (completed) — introduced `RUN_LENGTH_CEILING = 2` and the
  decision-log run-length source this item makes leadership-independent.
- **WL-0MWKY141H002LULI** — *Record per-project fairness metric on dispatch
  decisions* (completed) — added `selectedRoot` / `dispatchingRoot` /
  `consecutiveRunLength`, the evidence this item audits.
- **WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD** — *Docs: the enforced fair-scheduling rule and its
  metric* (completed) — the *Counting rules* section this item corrects.
- **WL-0MVKNC28B003UOLX** — *herdr: retain 24h of downtime dispatcher decision
  history* (completed) — the rotation/retention policy; its documented ≥ 24 h
  claim is contradicted by the measured ≈2.2 h/generation rate (AC4).
- **WL-0MWO38U4W002853V** — *Publish fairness report and update documentation*
  (blocked/intake_complete) — downstream consumer; the doc corrections here
  should feed it rather than bypass it.
- **WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7** — *downtime-worker.ts is a god class*
  (completed) and **WL-0MVLII1AO007TTRK** — *Extract downtime-worker
  coordination modules* (completed) — the module boundaries the chosen source
  must respect.
- **WL-0MWNYIL3Y0093GY0** — *Fairness across remote dispatching hosts*
  (open/plan_complete) — a machine-scoped ledger (Option B) must not preclude a
  future multi-host ledger; note the interaction when choosing.
- **WL-0MWO37XKC000FUKF** — *Root-cause analysis: identify mechanisms causing
  slot imbalance* (blocked/intake_complete) — may consume AC5's attribution.
- Repo docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — *Counting rules*,
  *Run-length source: the decision-log tail*, *Retention & rotation*.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Design churn risk.** Introducing a machine-scoped ledger (Option B) adds a
  second source of truth, which the original design deliberately rejected. The
  mitigation is AC1's explicit recording of the decision and trade-off, plus
  keeping the ledger write inside the existing coordination-lock critical
  section (no extra lock acquisition) and reading it fail-open.
- **Multi-host interaction.** A machine-scoped run ledger is per-machine; if
  remote dispatching hosts ever share roots (WL-0MWNYIL3Y0093GY0) the ledger
  must be keyed on the same project identity the round-robin cursor uses.
- **Retention vs disk.** Increasing `COORDINATION_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES` /
  `MAX_ROTATED_FILES` trades disk for auditability; AC4 permits documenting the
  limitation instead, which is the lower-risk option if the size caps are
  load-bearing.
- **Rotation-rate discrepancy.** The AC states ≈6.5 h for 4 generations, but the
  discovered-from measurement recorded ≈2.2 h per 500-line generation, i.e.
  ≈8.8 h for four generations. The retained window must therefore be
  **re-measured and stated as a measurement**, not assumed from either figure.
- **Small-sample attribution.** The two runs are historical and their decision
  rows are already rotated away, so AC5 may legitimately conclude "cannot be
  re-derived from retained evidence" — but the conclusion must still name which
  gate *could* have held each peer offer, and the rotation limitation must be
  recorded rather than glossed.
- **No gate changes.** The bound is an ordering rule; a change that turns it
  into a refusal would break parent AC1 and must be refused.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Additional fairness findings (e.g. `selectedRoot` ≠
  `dispatchingRoot` accounting, remote-host fairness, slot-imbalance RCA) are
  recording, not absorbing — they stay with their existing linked items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No interview questions were asked.** The item arrived from a completed
  read-only measurement with a problem statement, an explicit user story, seven
  measurable acceptance criteria, constraints, an impact statement and a
  predicted key-file list; per the intake contract the seed context sufficed to
  draft the brief, so the interview was skipped.

- **Q: Is this a duplicate of the completed run-length fix
  (WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O)?** — Answer (agent research, source:
  `wl show WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O --json`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fairness.ts`):
  No. That item *introduced* the whole-set rotation and the run-length bound
  sourced from the decision-log tail. This item fixes a defect **in that
  implementation** — the source is the leader's own root-scoped log, so a
  leadership hand-off resets the run to `1`. Partial overlap (same files, same
  mechanism) but a distinct gap; no rewrite needed.

- **Q: Is this a duplicate of the validation measurement
  (WL-0MWNN84HO004DXQU)?** — Answer (agent research): No. That item is
  read-only and explicitly forbade a dispatcher fix; its AC requires a *follow-up
  work item* for the failure. This item is that follow-up and carries the fix.

- **Q: Which run-length source should be adopted (cross-generation read,
  machine-scoped ledger, durable cursor)?** — Answer (agent research, source:
  `readPreviousDispatchRun` caller in
  `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` line ~500 and
  `~/.herdr/downtime/` contents): deliberately left to implementation by the
  item's own AC1, which requires the choice and its cost/lock trade-off to be
  recorded. The brief records the three candidates and notes that a plain
  cross-generation read cannot satisfy AC1 (the log stays per-leader-root),
  while a machine-scoped ledger fits the existing machine-dir + coordination-lock
  architecture. **Recorded as a decision for the implementer, not an open
  producer question.**

- **Q: Is `bug` the right issue type and `high` the right priority?** — Answer
  (agent decision): `bug` — the delivered guarantee is measurably incorrect
  (two runs of 3 against a ceiling of 2), not a missing capability. `high` —
  it is a fairness defect the operator escalated from a validation item and it
  blocks confidence in the parent epic's AC5; not `critical` because dispatch
  still proceeds and no data is lost.

- **Q: Does this item block or is it blocked by anything?** — Answer (agent
  research, source: `wl dep list WL-0MWT3Z9M9002Z9BF --json`): it carries a
  `depends-on` edge to **WL-0MWNN84HO004DXQU** (the measurement that produced
  the evidence). No inbound dependents were found; **WL-0MWO38U4W002853V**
  (publish the fairness report) is blocked for unrelated reasons and may
  consume the doc corrections later. No new dependency edges were added, so
  re-running this intake is idempotent.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSXHA1B0005G3E5** – Implement leader-only dispatch logic (completed)
- **WL-0MWJE9MIR005SBQK** – Advertise audit-lease capability and refuse old peers (open)
- **WL-0MTJPYM53003ORCV** – Downtime dispatcher: make wl-error pauses debuggable (log per-strike stderr/exitCode/timeout and probe context) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mvf3f9a7000hkp7, 0mvknc28b003uolx, 0mwke9vf800101v9, 0mwky141h002luli, 0mwky1839000jm5o (+494 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mvf3f9a7000hkp7, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+444 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: ac2, act, actually, added, additional (+361 more)

## Description

`wl delete` runs an auto-sync after a successful mutation, but the internal `performSync` call does **not** forward the project's `syncAllowedAuthors` allow-list (nor the derived `allowForeignAuthor`) from `getSyncDefaults()`. The author-identity gate therefore runs in strict mode and refuses any incoming commit whose author is not the local `user.email` — even when the project explicitly allow-lists that identity for `wl sync`.

**Root cause:** `src/commands/delete.ts` (~line 298) builds the `performSync` options from `getSyncDefaults()` but only passes `gitRemote` and `gitBranch`, dropping `allowedAuthors` and `allowForeignAuthor`. The CLI `wl sync` command (`src/commands/sync.ts` ~line 800-834) correctly forwards both, which is why explicit syncs honour the allow-list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl delete` auto-sync forwards `allowedAuthors` (and `allowForeignAuthor`) from `getSyncDefaults()` into `performSync`, so a commit authored by an allow-listed identity merges without refusal.
- Strict mode is preserved: when the config has no allow-list (or `syncAllowedAuthors: []`), a foreign-author commit is still refused by delete auto-sync, and the existing warning is still printed on refusal.
- The empty-author-email gate is unchanged: an allow-list can never admit an empty author.
- The "sync failure must not abort the delete" contract is preserved: a genuine refusal still warns and leaves the local mutation intact.
- `--no-sync` still skips the auto-sync entirely.
- The delete regression tests (`tests/cli/delete-auto-sync-allow-list.test.ts`) pass.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` option contract is unchanged (no breaking change to the CLI sync path).

## Implementation Notes

In `src/commands/delete.ts`, in the auto-sync block:

```ts
const defaults = getSyncDefaults(config || undefined);
await performSync(dataPath, utils.getDatabase, {
  file: dataPath,
  prefix: options.prefix,
  gitRemote: defaults.gitRemote,
  gitBranch: defaults.gitBranch,
  allowedAuthors: defaults.allowedAuthors,        // <-- add
  allowForeignAuthor: defaults.allowForeignAuthor, // <-- add
  push: true,
  dryRun: false,
  silent: true,
  isJsonMode,
  isVerbose: false,
});
```

`performSync` already accepts both fields in its options interface (`src/commands/sync.ts` lines 76-77).

## Deliverables

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — forward `allowedAuthors` / `allowForeignAuthor` from `getSyncDefaults()` into the auto-sync `performSync` call
- Code comment documenting why the allow-list is forwarded (parity with `wl sync`)

**Key Files:**

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — the fix (auto-sync `performSync` call, ~line 298)
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `getSyncDefaults()` and `performSync` options interface
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync-allow-list.test.ts` — regression tests (from test feature)

## Description

Update documentation to reflect that `wl delete` and `wl undelete` auto-sync honours the project's `syncAllowedAuthors` allow-list, exactly as `wl sync` does.

The bug (WL-0MWRQYK3X007RQ1T) caused a false identity-gate refusal on every delete/restore in a store where the remote carries commits from an allow-listed non-local identity. The fix makes the auto-sync forward the allow-list; the docs must state this parity so operators do not mistake a future refusal for a misconfiguration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` documents that `wl delete` and `wl undelete` auto-sync honours `syncAllowedAuthors` and `allowForeignAuthor`, with the same strict-mode and empty-author-email semantics as `wl sync`.
- `docs/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` notes the failure mode this fixes: an auto-sync refusal that does NOT abort the mutation and leaves the change unpushed until a manual `wl sync`.
- Code comments in `src/commands/delete.ts` and `src/commands/undelete.ts` explain why the allow-list is forwarded (parity with `wl sync`) and why the gate is not widened (`getSyncDefaults()` only derives `allowForeignAuthor: true` from the legacy `syncAllowForeignAuthor: true` key; `syncAllowedAuthors: []` stays strict).
- Any related docs (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `./CLI.md`, `docs/tutorials/02-team-collaboration.md`) that describe delete/undelete sync behaviour are cross-checked; update only where the allow-list parity is materially relevant.
- Documentation changes are accurate for both the allow-listed and strict configurations.

## Deliverables

- `docs/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` — parity note for delete/undelete auto-sync
- Code comment updates in `src/commands/delete.ts` and `src/commands/undelete.ts` (delivered with the fixes)
- Cross-check of `./CLI.md` / `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` / `docs/tutorials/02-team-collaboration.md`

**Key Files:**

- `docs/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` — primary documentation update
- `./CLI.md` — delete/undelete command reference (cross-check)
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — sync architecture (cross-check)
- `docs/tutorials/02-team-collaboration.md` — sync tutorial (cross-check)
- `src/commands/delete.ts`, `src/commands/undelete.ts` — code comments

## Parent

WL-0MWTAD9NV000IVK5 — Allow 2x implement/audit budget while panes wait for a model to be re-enabled. Covers parent AC9.

Depends on the admission wiring item. Write the tests first inside this item (the observable surfaces are cheap to assert and would otherwise be unpinned).

## Scope

Make relief visible and auditable: decision-log evidence, a `budget-relief` decision token and the effective cap on every operator surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An admission with relief records `budgetRelief: { kind, baseCap, effectiveCap, blockedPaneIds, reason, until }`; a refusal at/above the effective cap records the same shape with the observed `live` figure. No relief ⇒ no `budgetRelief` key (the pre-change entry shape is unchanged).
- `until` is the earliest `cooldownUntil` among the blocked panes of that kind; `reason` is a stable token (`model-cooldown`) with the unreadable-signal variant (`model-cooldown-unreadable`) when the read failed closed.
- `budget-relief` is added to the decision-log vocabulary in `downtime-log-budget.ts` and emitted alongside the decision entry (never as a refusal token).
- The worklist header counter renders the effective cap and marks relief (e.g. `[budget: implement 6/10 relief · audit 0/1]`): no segment for an uncapped kind, no relief marker when relief is inactive, and nothing rendered when the budget is unavailable.
- The stderr skip line (`hostBudgetSkipLine`) reports the effective cap when relief is active, and the configured cap otherwise.
- Table-driven tests written first cover: relief admission evidence, refusal-above-effective-cap evidence, absent-evidence case, unreadable-signal evidence, header rendering with and without relief, and the skip line.
- Existing observability suites (`host-budget-status.test.ts`, `host-budget-observability.test.ts`, `downtime-log.test.ts`) stay green.

- Delivered parent criterion (WL-0MWTAD9NV000IVK5): Decision-log evidence `budgetRelief: { kind, baseCap, effectiveCap, blockedPaneIds, reason, until }` is recorded on an admission with relief and on a refusal above the effective cap; a `budget-relief` header/decision token is added to the vocabulary; the worklist counter shows `n/effectiveCap`.

## Key Files

## Goal

Clear the `needsProducerReview` flag on the prep item(s) that the producer-review provenance audit proves clearable, so a stale flag stops hiding otherwise-dispatchable prep work from the dispatcher's plan/intake fallback.

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD (Scope item 4a). Discovered-from: WL-0MWTBJEI2008UGUR.

## Owner / queue

- **Owner:** dispatcher maintainer / operator (agent-executable run; producer sign-off recorded before clearing).
- **Queue:** ContextHub `herdr` maintenance; targets the audit's active roots (`ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`, `SorraAgents`, `tce-the-rising`).

## Evidence rows that justify this item

From the AC2 provenance audit (comment `WL-C0MWTTIOEN000M9LN` on WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` -> *Recorded producer-review provenance audit*):

| row | root | id | flag source | deciding evidence | open question | group |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | AI_Hell | AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P | `manual` | none (dependency-held) | no | `can-clear-now` |

Group counts at `--now 2026-11-23T22:15:00Z`: **1 can clear now, 17 need producer input**. The single clearable row is independently held by six unmet dependencies, so clearing it cannot cause a dispatch. This item covers only that `can-clear-now` grouping; the 17 `needs-producer-input` rows are batched separately (follow-up 4b).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Re-run the provenance classification (`classifyProducerReviewProvenance` / `assembleProducerReviewProvenance`, or the documented `--now` read) and record the live `can-clear-now` set at execution time; the audit's row 5 (`AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P`) is the expected seed.
2. Clear the flag (`wl --worklog-dir <root>/.worklog update <id> --needs-producer-review false`) only on rows grouped `can-clear-now`; no row grouped `needs-producer-input` is cleared.
3. For every cleared row, add a comment naming the deciding evidence, the provenance source and the independent hold (if any), so the clear is auditable — never a silent clear.
4. Re-read the flagged set after the run and record `before -> after` counts per root; the `needs-producer-input` set is unchanged.
5. Record on WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD the ids cleared (or "none" with the live reason) and the evidence.
6. No gate, budget, dispatcher-selection or skill change; no item reassigned; no dispatch marker written.

## Dependency

Depends on the provenance audit's `can-clear-now` grouping (WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI).

## Duplicate check

Searched `wl search "needsProducerReview stale flag clear"`, `wl search "clear stale needsProducerReview"`, `wl search "stale producer review flag"` and reviewed the related ids. Matches are the completed provenance audit (WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI) and flag-mechanism items (WL-0MV82CHGQ000HAZZ, WL-0MTIAL65N004T22F, WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0); none performs the clearing run. No duplicate.

## Impact

A stale producer-review flag stops parking a prep item behind an operator question it no longer has, so the dispatcher can offer it again.

## Goal

- **Queue:** implement (skill change) in SorraAgents. This ContextHub item is the coordination item; the actual skill edit lands in SorraAgents (do not edit the symlinked `~/.pi/agent/skills/` from a ContextHub worktree).

## Evidence rows that justify this item

- AC2 provenance audit (comment `WL-C0MWTTIOEN000M9LN`): **16 of 18** flagged prep rows are sourced `question-loop`, i.e. a clarifying question set the hold.
- Concrete rows: `AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY` (intake Q1–Q3 posted, marked `OPEN QUESTION`), `WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG` (intake recorded its own recommendation, then set the handoff), `AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X` ("remains open for the producer"), plus the `SA-…`/`RISE-…` rows in the audit table.

- Root cause item 4: producer review is a real but minority contributor (18/416 = 4.3 %), so this change targets recurrence, not the 2026-11-22/23 empty bucket.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Define, in the shared interview contract, the distinction between a routine question the agent resolves itself (research/assumption, recorded in the Appendix) and a genuine producer handoff (a decision only the producer can make).
2. Update `interview/SKILL.md` §4, `plan/SKILL.md`'s producer-review section and `intake/SKILL.md`'s handoff so `wl reviewed <id> true` is used only for a genuine handoff; routine questions record the assumption/answer and continue.
3. Add a positive/negative test (or skill fixture) asserting a routine self-resolved question does **not** set the flag and a genuine handoff **does**.
4. Add the rationale and a worked example to the skill docs; no dispatcher or gate change.
5. Land the change in the skills' source repo (SorraAgents `skill/`), not by editing the symlinked `~/.pi/agent/skills/` in place; create/link the SorraAgents implementation item at run start.
6. Record the change and commit on this item and on WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD.

## Goal

Make the producer-review provenance audit a packaged, repeatable read-only command so a re-run cannot drift from the dispatcher predicates the way the manual 2026-11-23 audit did (discovered-from:WL-0MWTVPJAN003GLAV).

## Problem statement

The provenance rule exists as pure, tested code (`classifyProducerReviewProvenance` / `assembleProducerReviewProvenance`), but nothing packages it into a runnable command: every audit is a one-off script that re-collects comments, audit records, dispatch markers and dependency edges by hand. The recorded 2026-11-23 audit (WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI) demonstrates the failure mode — for `AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P` it supplied `dependency` as an independent hold from six **inbound `depended-on-by`** edges instead of outbound `depends-on` edges, so the live re-run regraded the row `needs-producer-input`. A wrongful clear was avoided only because the clearing follow-up happened to re-check the live set first.

## Users

- **Dispatcher maintainer / operator** — needs to answer "which prep items are producer-review flagged, why, how old is that evidence, and which can be cleared now?" for any root at any (including past) instant, without writing code.
- **Remediation agent** (downtime worker or `implement` session) — needs a diff-stable machine payload it can quote as the seed evidence set for a clearing run.

User stories:

- As a dispatcher maintainer, I want one command that reports every prep-stage `needsProducerReview=true` row per root with its flag source, deciding evidence, age, open question and holds, so that a stale flag is distinguishable from a live producer question.
- As a remediation agent, I want a deterministic `--now` replay whose holds come from the dispatcher's own predicates, so that the `can-clear-now` set I clear is provably safe to clear.
- As a reviewer, I want byte-identical output for the same `--now`, so that two audits of the same window can be diffed in review.

## Context

The provenance rule lives in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` (pure functions: plain data in, verdict out — no `wl` call, no subprocess, no file write) and is documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` → *Producer-review provenance*, with the recorded audit in *Recorded producer-review provenance audit (2026-11-23 22:15Z)* and the clearing run in *Stale-flag clearing run*.

The prep-supply read already has an equivalent packaged command — `packages/herdr/src/prep-supply-report-cli.ts`, published as the `worklog-prep-supply` bin — which owns argument parsing, root resolution, output and an injected read-only I/O seam, plus a documented section (*Prep-supply report command*). Provenance has no equivalent, so every audit re-implements the read side, which is exactly where the edge direction was got wrong. This item mirrors the prep-supply command's shape for provenance rather than inventing a new one.

## Existing state

- `downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` (521 lines) exports `PRODUCER_REVIEW_SOURCES`, `PRODUCER_REVIEW_GROUPS`, `ProducerReviewProvenanceInput` / `Verdict` / `Table`, `classifyProducerReviewProvenance`, `assembleProducerReviewProvenance` and `formatProducerReviewAge`. `ProducerReviewProvenanceInput.holds` already accepts the gate tokens (`dependency`, `assignee-hold`, `startOn`, `attempt-budget`, `cooldown`, `dispatch-marker`) but nothing populates them from live reads.
- Holding/predicate logic already exists and must be **reused, not restated**: `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (`downtime-worker.gates.ts`) for `assignee-hold` / `startOnNotReached` / `not-dispatchable`, `parseDepListBlockersOutput` (`downtime-worker.parsers.ts`) which keeps only outbound `direction === 'depends-on'` edges, and `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` / `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` for the worker-side gates.
- The read side already exists as an injected seam: `createPrepSupplyReportDeps()` (`downtime-worker.prep-supply-source.ts`) wires the consolidated `wl worklist --json` read, the per-root `wl list --json` fallback per prep stage, batched dependency edges (in-process with a per-item `wl dep list --json` fallback) and the rolling dispatch log (`<root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`).
- That seam has **no comment or stored-audit read** — the classifier's two remaining evidence sources have no helper: comments come from `wl show <id> --json` and the stored audit record from `wl audit-show <id> --json`. Only `auditResult` (the item-level mirror on `wl show`) is currently reachable, and the rule requires the stored record's `readyToClose`/`generatedAt`.
- No provenance audit command, bin entry or docs section exists.

## Desired change

A new read-only command (source + built bin, following the prep-supply pattern) that, for every prep-stage item carrying `needsProducerReview=true` on each requested root, emits one provenance row: `id`, `root`, `source`, deciding evidence reference, flag age, open question, holds, group — as a human table plus a per-root JSON payload. Holds are computed from the dispatcher/gate predicates over **outbound** `depends-on` edges only. `--root` (repeatable) and `--now` (ISO-8601) allow an exact replay; output is sorted and byte-stable.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A read-only command/diagnostic emits per-root JSON plus a human table of provenance rows (`id`, source, deciding evidence reference, flag age, open question, holds, group) for every prep-stage `needsProducerReview=true` item.
2. Holds are derived from the dispatcher/gate predicates (outbound non-terminal `depends-on` edges, `assignee`, `startOn`, attempt budget, cooldown, dispatch marker), never from inbound edges; a regression test pins that an inbound `depended-on-by` edge is not a hold.
3. `--root` (repeatable) and `--now` are supported for a deterministic replay; output is stable and diffable.
4. Strictly read-only: no flag, assignee or marker mutation (regression test).
5. Usage and the `--now`/hold semantics are documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`; changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes.

## Constraints

- **Read-only, proven not asserted.** No `wl update`, no `wl reviewed`, no marker write, no `getDefaultSettingsPath()` (it `mkdir`s the config dir); registry path resolution follows the prep-supply command's pure-read approach.
- **One source of truth for holds.** Reuse `classifyItemForDispatchDetail`, `parseDepListBlockersOutput`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` and `isNonTerminalCooldownActive`; do not fork a second copy of any predicate.
- **Fail closed.** An unreadable root or unparseable payload is reported as an error (named on stderr, exit `1`), never rendered as an empty healthy row set — mirroring the prep-supply exit-code contract (`0` success, `1` partial root failure, `2` usage/no roots).
- **Stable ordering.** Roots sorted by path, rows by item id; `flagAgeMs: null` renders as `unknown` via `formatProducerReviewAge`, never as a fabricated age.
- **UK English** in code comments, docs and output copy.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Wrong-direction edges (the discovered-from bug).** Mitigation: AC2's regression test plus reuse of `parseDepListBlockersOutput`, which already filters to `direction === 'depends-on'`.
- **Predicate drift.** The audit could pass its own tests while diverging from the live dispatcher. Mitigation: the command quotes predicate outputs rather than paraphrasing, and the docs section states the audit reads the dispatcher's predicates.
- **Accidental write.** Risk that a "helpful" code path clears or reassigns. Mitigation: AC4 regression test asserting item/flag state and the dispatch marker log are byte-identical before and after a run.
- **Scope creep.** Clearing flags (WL-0MWTVPJAN003GLAV), batching producer interviews, reassigning items and any dispatch/gate/skill behaviour change are **out of scope** and belong to their own items.
- **Read cost.** Comments and the stored audit record are per-item reads (`wl show`, `wl audit-show`), not part of the batched worklist pass. The bound is the flagged prep set (18 rows across four roots in the 2026-11-23 audit), so per-item reads are acceptable; the command must not fan out to every prep item.
- **Assumption:** prep-stage supply is `idea` + `intake_complete` (`PREP_SUPPLY_STAGES`), matching the recorded audit's population; the command reuses that constant rather than redefining the stage set.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.ts` — new pure collection/assembly layer: per-root rows for flagged prep items, populating `ProducerReviewProvenanceInput.holds` from the gate predicates.

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply-source.ts` — reuse `createPrepSupplyReportDeps()` as the read-only I/O seam; extend it (or add a sibling source module) with the two missing reads: `wl show <id> --json` for comments and `wl audit-show <id> --json` for the stored audit record.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parsers.ts` — `parseDepListBlockersOutput` (outbound `depends-on` only).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `classifyItemForDispatchDetail`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted`.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — new `bin` entry (`worklog-provenance-audit` → `dist/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-cli.js`).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — new `### Provenance audit command (WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P, child of WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD)` section after *Producer-review provenance*, modelled on *Prep-supply report command*.

## Related work

- **WL-0MWTBJ7G1004Y29B — Prep-supply report command** (completed). The direct template: same argument/root/`--now`/exit-code/read-only contract. This item mirrors its shape for provenance; it deliberately does *not* duplicate its buckets.

- **WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD — Prep backlog is almost entirely producer-review flagged** (open; the epic that both the recorded audit and the clearing run are children of). Scope item 4a's audit needs a repeatable runner.
- **WL-0MWTVPL1A005KB4D — Change intake/plan/interview skills so routine questions do not park items behind producer review** (open). Reduces future flag volume; independent of this command.
- **WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER — Batch producer interviews for prep items grouped needs-producer-input** (open). The sibling follow-up (4b): consumes the `needs-producer-input` group this command emits.
- **WL-0MVI0IS6Y0028KTO — Read cache: worklist invocation as one cache entry** (completed). Relevant if the command's per-item `wl show` / `wl audit-show` reads ever need caching; not required here (the flagged set is small).
- Docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` → *Producer-review provenance*, *Recorded producer-review provenance audit*, *Stale-flag clearing run*, *Prep-supply report command*.

No clarifying questions were needed: the seed description carried the goal, the failure that motivates it (the inbound-vs-outbound edge direction in `AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P`), the five acceptance criteria, the out-of-scope boundary and the impact.
